final.narration: Flow equals water speed times cross-sectional area (Q = V × A), which the curve assumes holds at each stage. Since the 2024-12-17 visit, measurements at the Pigeon River near Hepco, USGS 03459500, sat 33 % below the rating. The river stands 0.33 ft higher for the same flow, carrying 150 cfs (26 %) less at 2.33 ft. The hydrographer noted "Scour control changed" on 2024-12-17. In the note's terms, the control (the riffle just downstream that sets the water level) eroded, so the same flow passes at a lower level. That disagrees with the data. Area changed -11 % and speed -22 %, so flow at the same level changed about -31 %, which agrees with the -26 % change. Hurricane Helene (2024-09-27) passed between the 2024-08-22 and 2024-12-17 visits; no gauging was made during the storm. Possible lead: Duke Energy opened floodgates at Walters Dam to release surging Pigeon River waters during Hurricane Helene (Walters hydro plant turns 100: Dam, powerhouse withstood Helene's onslaught).
